alternativeComparison: D18-single-a protects expertise by directing a real engineer. This alternative claims expertise through destructive inspection, with B's audition and the panel's property increasing the stakes.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We disagree about dinner. First to peel five potatoes chooses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we just order pizza?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whoever finds the best deal wins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to compete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the most convincing case. I'll judge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns dinner disagreement into a peeling race, A3 makes B2's pizza solution competitive, and A5 makes refusal another contest A controls.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies pizza and therefore deal-finding in A3; B4 rejects competition and therefore becomes the subject of A5's judged argument.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a practical compromise and B4 states a boundary; both change the form of A's competition.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from competing over dinner to judging whether B can escape competition, increasing A's control.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner planning and five potatoes; A3 uses the recognizable task of finding a pizza deal.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'I'll judge' efficiently reveals how A intends to control the outcome of B4's objection.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns dinner preference into a pre-rigged peeling race; A3 declares a price victory; A5 changes the contest and selects a favorable judge.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cheaper-dinner condition supplies A3's price contest; B4's free-pizza voucher forces A5 to compete on quality instead.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants pizza within a cost condition and B4 produces a voucher, actively removing A's claimed advantage.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4's price tie into cooking two dinners and recruiting Mum as a judge whose preference favors A.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies potatoes, pizza and four already-peeled potatoes; A5 establishes the shared family connection through Mum's preferences.

brevityWit.evidence: A1's 'I've done four' immediately reveals the rigging; A5's favorable judge repeats that intention with a larger commitment.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers a price condition; A3 declares the already-owned potatoes a zero-cost winner.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 makes pizza equally free; A5 switches to a judged taste contest and nominates a sympathetic judge.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly turns differences into contests and chooses rules that give A an advantage.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 commits both people to producing competing dinners and brings family preference into the attempt to win.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D19 makes A convert dinner preferences and proposed compromises into competitions selected to give A a winning advantage.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General competitiveness could merely organize contests; A explicitly chooses a head start, claims a price victory, and proposes a judge who favors A's cooking.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 announces four potatoes already peeled, A3 declares victory over B2's price criterion, and A5 uses B4's free pizza to create a taste contest with a favorable judge.

recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected candidate to establish intended victory in every contest and let B materially challenge the advantage. The dinner setting remains; a voucher and Mum's judging role are new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A1, A3 and A5 each specify an expected route to winning; logic 5, because B2's price challenge causes A3's existing-stock claim and B4's free voucher causes A5's taste contest; relationship 4, because B2 bargains for pizza and B4 defeats A's cost advantage; heightening 4, because A5 proposes making both meals and recruiting a favorable judge; specificity 5, from A1's four peeled potatoes and B4's voucher; brevity/wit 4, as A5's remembered praise reveals why Mum should judge. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; B and Mum remain uncommitted. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
remainingConcern: A1 announces the rigged competition very explicitly, and A5's biased judge is predictable, but both remain clear and playable. No rewrite needed.
writerReservation: A3 treats food already purchased as free, which is self-serving character accounting. Mum's preference appears only in A5, although it directly explains the new competitive tactic.
alternativeComparison: The preserved tea alternative changes scoring after a completed loss; this version builds a new contest after a tie and tries to control its adjudication.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea is stronger than yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used the same teapot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I poured more decisively.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drink it faster and we can settle that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asserts superiority, A3 invents a new basis after B2 disproves it, and A5 proposes racing after B4 dismisses the comparison.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's shared pot to switch to pouring; A5 answers B4's dismissal with speed, though 'settle that' has a loose referent.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the premise and B4 minimizes the topic, but B has no concrete want beyond deflating A's claims.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes verbal superiority into a proposed drinking contest after B4 rejects the significance of tea.

specificity.evidence: A1 and B2 establish two cups from one teapot, giving A3 a specific factual obstacle.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's decisive pouring is a compact invented distinction; A5 is brief but does not clearly declare how A expects to win.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes milk preference a superiority claim; A3 and A5 change the contest to criteria A expects to win.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 defeats the strength distinction and introduces speed; B4 defeats speed and introduces refills, which A5 immediately exploits.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains a practical preference and B4 continues breakfast, forcing A to compete with B's ordinary choices.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts the two mouthfuls used for a speed advantage in A3 into an all-breakfast endurance commitment after losing.

specificity.evidence: A1's tea, B2's shared teapot and A3's two remaining mouthfuls create precise, playable continuity.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 reverses the purpose of the same two mouthfuls, making the comic turn depend exactly on B4's finished cup.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B removes tea strength as a distinction and mentions drinking sooner; A switches to a race with an apparent head start.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B has already finished and is refilling; A changes victory to avoiding refills.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A chooses and revises competitive criteria to ensure personal victory over ordinary differences.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A commits to prolonging breakfast with two mouthfuls solely to rescue a losing position.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D19 makes A turn a difference in tea preferences into a contest and change the winning criterion when B's progress defeats A's expected advantage.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Boasting alone would assert superior taste; A repeatedly proposes measurable competitions whose terms offer A a route to victory.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B2's reason for adding milk causes A3's finishing race; B4's completed cup and planned refill cause A5 to compete over needing fewer refills.

recommendedEdit: Rebuilt the causal exchange into five spoken ABABA turns, retaining the tea setting and specifying breakfast. B2 introduces speed, which A3 makes a race A expects to win with only two mouthfuls remaining. B4 defeats that expectation and supplies the refill that A5 makes the new competitive disadvantage. Every original firstPass score and evidence string is preserved. Acceptance remains for the required fresh reviewer.
remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. B's relationship to A is unspecified, but shared breakfast supplies sufficient interaction.
writerReservation: A5 openly changes the scoring after losing the first proposed race; the tactic is deliberately unfair, and B can challenge it. B's practical wish to enjoy another cup supplies resistance without an explicit argument.
alternativeComparison: Unlike a's demand that B participate, b reveals winning intent through increasingly self-serving rule changes.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No pressure from venue management!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've lost the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Nothing left tying us to the past.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats zero sales as rehearsal time, A3 celebrates cancellation, and A5 welcomes the lost deposit as liberation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 removes the venue and A3 welcomes freedom from management; B4 adds financial loss and A5 recasts it as severing the remaining tie.

relationship.evidence: A1's 'our show' and B4's 'We've lost' establish shared stakes, while B keeps confronting A with increasingly costly facts.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from the relief of A3 to 'Wonderful' at losing money, sustaining greater optimism under worse professional consequences.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an unsold show, B2 a theatre cancellation, and B4 a forfeited deposit.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 and A5 are economical reversals of the exact losses B reports; A5's freedom claim grows from the vanished deposit.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns no audience into rehearsal freedom, A3 turns cancellation into a populated venue, and A5 turns near-total loss of funds into a touring production.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's cancellation and deposit request inform A3's replacement venue; B4's retained deposit and bus-only budget directly produce A5's performance between stops.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries to recover funds and B4 states the remaining travel budget; A5 recruits this practical collaborator into carrying the show onward.

heightening.evidence: B4 leaves only bus fare, and A5 increases the artistic claim from a substitute pub venue to a touring production using that bus.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an unsuccessful show; B2's deposit and A5's scenery and exact change make the resource problem and proposed next step concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'People already go there voluntarily' follows the empty-house setback; A5's touring claim is earned by B4's bus fare.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 removes the theatre and seeks the deposit; A3 imagines using recovered funds for a pub venue with existing patrons.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 removes the deposit and identifies the bus as their only affordable option; A5 transforms that very transport into the next performance venue.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Each loss leads A to a more ambitious positive interpretation and an actionable continuation.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 promotes the dwindling show into a touring production precisely when the budget permits only going home.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D20 makes A greet worsening theatrical losses with increasingly ambitious opportunities built from whatever resources B says remain.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Selling a disastrous plan would insist that it is responsible or unavoidable; A instead welcomes each setback as opening a more exciting possibility.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 celebrates B2's cancellation as access to a pub audience; after B4 removes the hire budget and leaves only bus fare, A5 enthusiastically promotes the journey home into a touring production.

recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected abstract liberation into concrete optimistic plans that B's financial information changes. The unsold show, cancellation and lost deposit remain; the pub and bus are new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A3 welcomes cancellation and A5 celebrates having only bus fare as a touring opportunity; logic 5, because B2's proposed refund enables A3's venue idea and B4's lost funds and bus journey supply A5's replacement; relationship 4, because B2 pursues reimbursement and B4 establishes their remaining means; heightening 4, because A5 expands a failed stationary show into a proposed tour and volunteers to carry scenery; specificity 5, from B4's fare limit and A5's performance between stops; brevity/wit 4, because A5's grand touring claim depends on the mundane journey home. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; no performance or audience response is fixed. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
remainingConcern: A3 assumes a suitable pub space, and A5's scenery is newly introduced, but neither disrupts the established theatrical situation. No rewrite needed.
writerReservation: A's proposed bus performance may be unwelcome or impractical; the dialogue leaves it as sincere enthusiasm rather than an accomplished event. The scenery must be imagined as portable for A5's offer to be playable.
alternativeComparison: The breakfast alternative preserves a pleasant shared activity through practical setbacks; this version scales up artistic ambition as the practical means shrink.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss the dent in your car, I've found a lovely garage café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you hit a bollard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their scones are enormous. Shall I book a table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does the booking need a mechanic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent question. Let's inspect their staffing over tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 dodges B2's bollard question through scones, and A5 diverts B4 into staffing, although A1 openly names the dent.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 avoids answering B2 coherently, but B4 assumes a booking requires a mechanic when A3 offered only a café table.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks accountability for damage to B's car, and B4 tries to connect A's hospitality to a repair.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats the tea diversion after B4 without making the forbidden topic appreciably harder to avoid.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes car damage and a garage café; A3's table booking is playable, though B4's mechanic lacks setup.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's enormous scones are a clear diversion; A5's 'inspect their staffing' sounds constructed to service B4's unexplained mechanic.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 avoids B2's question about the car; A5 counters B4's inspection with another breakfast-focused diversion.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 triggers A3's toast distraction; B4's plan to inspect the car prompts A5's bus-and-cocktails alternative.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants an explanation for work on B's car and B4 takes initiative to discover it directly.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands A3's conversational distraction into a proposal controlling travel and shared activity.

specificity.evidence: A1 naturally joins a garage booking to its café; A3 exploits B's known enthusiasm for unlimited toast.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's breakfast cocktails extend A3's food lure and provide a motivated reason to abandon driving.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B asks why repairs are needed; A substitutes a personalized account of the café breakfast.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B plans to inspect the car alone; A proposes shared bus travel and cocktails to keep B engaged elsewhere.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Avoidance of the car's condition motivates both the food pitch and the transportation proposal.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A moves from changing the subject to trying to prevent an independent inspection.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D14 makes A repeatedly steer conversation and immediate plans away from one forbidden subject as B approaches it.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Helpful Culprit would make A investigate the car damage; this A uses hospitality to prevent the damage becoming the topic.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 answers B2's garage question with toast, and A5 responds to B4's inspection plan by proposing transport that avoids the car.

recommendedEdit: Kept the garage-café setting and removed the unsupported mechanic booking. Second internal pass: fidelity 5, logic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 4, brevity 4; total 90. B4 threatens direct discovery, causing A5 to extend the diversion from conversation to the journey itself.
remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. Taking the bus does not itself prevent B inspecting the car; A5 remains an attempted diversion.
writerReservation: The damage is now implied by the unexplained garage booking; A5 only proposes delaying inspection and cannot guarantee B will cooperate.
alternativeComparison: Alternative a uses personalized enticement and practical arrangements; b jumps between visible distractions.

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't read that letter yet. Have you noticed the new curtains?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says the rent's overdue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Think how much these curtains improve the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How much did they cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at that bird outside. Perfectly framed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open that rent letter yet. Help me hang our new curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He'll love how we're looking after the place. Let's get a photo of the curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send him one and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet showing. Let's rearrange the room first. You move the sofa; I'll hold your phone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 steers away from the letter, A3 evades B2's overdue-rent disclosure, and A5 changes subject again when B4 asks about spending.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 returns to the curtains after B2 identifies rent; B4 makes those curtains financially dangerous, causing A5 to move attention through the window.

relationship.evidence: B2 reads the consequential letter despite A's diversion, and B4 follows the money through A's chosen alternative subject.

heightening.evidence: B4 turns A's safe curtain topic into a spending question, forcing A5 into a more conspicuous second escape.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a letter and new curtains; B2 locates the financial problem and A5 uses the established window area.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Perfectly framed' carries the curtains into the new bird diversion, making the escape connected rather than wholly random.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delays the rent letter through curtains; A3 diverts the landlord's deadline into a photograph; A5 diverts the arrears inquiry into rearranging furniture.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's required landlord response inspires A3's photo response; B4 repurposes that photo to ask about arrears, causing A5 to delay photography and claim the phone.

relationship.evidence: B2 insists on today's deadline and B4 combines A's decorating idea with the necessary inquiry, actively defeating A's first diversion.

heightening.evidence: After B4 turns the photo into a route to the forbidden subject, A5 escalates to moving the sofa and taking custody of B's phone.

specificity.evidence: A1 naturally establishes shared housing, a rent letter and new curtains; A5 gives actors concrete furniture and a phone to negotiate over.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'I'll hold your phone' follows precisely from B4's plan to contact the landlord, earning the comic reveal of the practical diversion.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 introduces the landlord's deadline; A3 proposes a decorating photo as the apparent response.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 will send the photo and ask about arrears; A5 makes taking that photo contingent on rearranging the room and offers to hold the communication device.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: The rent-accountability subject explains each successive household diversion.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A moves from changing the topic to creating physical work and controlling access to the phone.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D14 makes A protect a forbidden topic by finding a new conversational exit whenever B brings the current diversion close to it.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General distractibility would not repeatedly move away from the same financial exposure.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 replaces B2's demand for a landlord response with a decorating photograph; when B4 connects that photograph to rent accountability, A5 substitutes furniture rearrangement and requests the phone.

recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected bird distraction into a consequential attempt to occupy B and delay communication. The unopened rent letter and curtains remain; the photo, carpet and furniture task are new. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, because A3 and A5 repeatedly evade rent accountability; logic 5, because B2's landlord demand motivates the photo and B4's proposed message motivates delaying it; relationship 4, because B2 has a deadline and B4 tries to use A's suggestion constructively; heightening 4, because A5 expands hanging curtains into rearranging the room and holding B's phone; specificity 5, from A1's shared home task and B2's deadline; brevity/wit 4, from A5's convenient division of labour. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; no compliance is forced. Original firstPass remains unchanged.
remainingConcern: A5 makes A's obstruction fairly transparent; it remains playable as sincere insistence on presenting the home properly. No rewrite needed.
writerReservation: A's concern about the carpet is transparently convenient. A5 proposes taking custody of the phone, but B remains free to send the message immediately. The D14 provenance mismatch remains unresolved.
alternativeComparison: The preserved car scene diverts inquiry through shared treats and transport; this scene uses domestic improvement and B's cooperative adaptation to increase the obstruction.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. Lovely. I'll fetch a cloth.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful coverage. You must be thrilled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you get the blue paint out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll start with the part that used to be my afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. Stay there; I'll get a cloth. We can fix this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep blotting. You're doing well. That carpet was my birthday present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's spreading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. Good catch. Take my clean shirt. I am absolutely furious, but you are not tackling this alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 offers a cloth, but A3's 'You must be thrilled' replaces encouragement with mockery.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's spreading paint; A5 barely uses B4's request to remove blue paint.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants practical cleanup, while A3 mainly ridicules B rather than helping.

heightening.evidence: A5 complains about the afternoon without developing the helpfulness or visibly increasing fury.

specificity.evidence: A1's painted sofa and B2's carpet establish an immediately playable domestic accident.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Wonderful coverage' is compact; A5's afternoon metaphor displaces the cleanup.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 pairs encouragement with the birthday carpet's loss; A5 supplies a shirt while declaring fury. The anger is more stated than enacted.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 extends the spill to the carpet, which A3 addresses; B4 discredits the cloth, so A5 substitutes a clean shirt.

relationship.evidence: B4 reports that the attempted repair is failing; A5 credits B's observation and maintains practical solidarity despite personal loss.

heightening.evidence: After B4, A5 sacrifices another possession to help, increasing A's commitment while the explicitly expressed anger rises.

specificity.evidence: A1 immediately establishes spilled paint on A's sofa; A3's birthday carpet and A5's clean shirt provide playable personal stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's encouragement beside the birthday-present detail earns the tension; A5's explicit emotional declaration explains some of the joke.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies the carpet as newly damaged; A3 directs blotting and reveals that carpet's sentimental value.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says the cloth spreads paint; A5 acknowledges the failure and offers a clean shirt instead.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 sustain practical help and encouragement while A's resentment becomes explicit fury.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5's willingness to sacrifice a shirt after the sofa and carpet makes continued support increasingly costly.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A must keep providing sincere help and encouragement as the same interaction makes A increasingly furious.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Sarcastic politeness can sound supportive while actually withdrawing encouragement and care.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Original A3 mocks B's satisfaction; revised A3 praises blotting and A5 supplies a shirt despite explicit fury.

recommendedEdit: Revised within the paint accident to restore simultaneous support and anger. Second internal pass: fidelity 5 (A3/A5 encourage through fury), logic 5 (B4's spreading cloth causes A5's shirt), relationship 4 (B2/B4 report worsening damage), heightening 4 (A5 sacrifices clothing), specificity 5 (A1 sofa cleanup), brevity 4 (A5 is direct but explicit): 92/100. Five spoken ABABA turns and the word limit pass.
remainingConcern: Accepted as supplied; no rewrite needed. The growing fury relies partly on A5 naming it, rather than on consistently escalating verbal strain.
writerReservation: A5 names fury directly; performance must also convey its increase without making the encouragement sarcastic.
alternativeComparison: Unlike the birthday chauffeur in D21-single-b, this A faces damage to personal possessions and offers increasingly costly physical help.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take your time choosing lunch. I'm delighted to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might look at another menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The parking meter loves exploring too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we go somewhere else?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll tell the meter it was only a relationship trial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the birthday lunch you really want. I'll drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds wasted. Fine. You love the sea; let's make a day of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another forty? Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. Give me the number. You're getting your sea view. Ask for a window; you deserve one.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 and A5 personify the meter sarcastically, with little sincere encouragement or increasing fury.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 prompts parking pressure in A3, but A5's 'relationship trial' adds little to B4's relocation request.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 express indecision; A's actual support remains largely the initial driving offer.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats the meter joke without increasing sacrifice or anger after B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes lunch and driving; A3 supplies a credible parking constraint.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'relationship trial' feels constructed around the meter rather than A's sincere objective.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 combines 'Forty pounds wasted' with encouragement; A5 escalates to 'bloody sandwich' while arranging the booking and affirming B deserves a window.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 identifies the lost deposit, which A3 resents but accepts; B4 adds another forty, directly producing A5's eighty-pound calculation and request for the number.

relationship.evidence: A1 gives B birthday choice; B2 chooses the sea and B4 commits by booking, increasing the cost of A's sincere support.

heightening.evidence: B4's additional payment makes A5 angrier and more actively helpful: A takes over the call while insisting on B's sea view.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes birthday lunch and driving; B2 and A3 locate the conflict in a seaside preference and an existing forty-pound deposit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich' earns its irritation from B4's payment request; the window encouragement sustains the contradiction.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2's seaside choice and forfeited deposit become A3's simultaneous resentment and encouragement to make a day of it.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The director's unavailable. Let's keep today's launch exactly as planned.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her office is empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A distraction-free leadership environment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has she resigned?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The launch still has a time. Let's protect that certainty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the director's name on the launch programme. The department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my drawer. Without her, they'll each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give them equal introductions; nobody inherits the microphone.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'distraction-free leadership environment' is a compact euphemism tied to B2's evidence.

hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from suppressing evidence to personally sustaining the director's symbolic presence.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who made it comfortable to sign?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director was consulted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Whose budget improves when the workshop disappears?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I tell the workshop staff they're closing, who backed your decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll name her approval. Who else supported it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then Sales can join the staff meeting. Who signed off on giving them our space?

responseLogic.evidence: A3 probes behind B2's personal signature; A5 follows B4's director disclosure with a budget inquiry, though it could use that director more directly.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims personal responsibility and B4 supplies consultation, but B's reason for limiting disclosure stays unclear.

heightening.evidence: A5 broadens inquiry to financial benefit after B4 without clearly increasing pressure on the newly named director.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes workshop closure and B2 a signed decision; A5 identifies a concrete budget trail.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Who made it comfortable to sign?' efficiently challenges B2's claim of solitary responsibility.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks for backers, A3 distinguishes approval from support, and A5 pursues authorization for the beneficiary's space transfer.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 names the approving director; A3 retains that attribution and seeks additional supporters.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 identifies Sales as supporter and beneficiary while requesting omission; A5 brings Sales into the meeting and probes the transfer approval.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A repeatedly separates supporters, authorizers and beneficiaries instead of accepting an anonymous institutional decision.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes the newly named beneficiary answerable in the affected staff's presence.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D64 drives A to trace a position through its supporters, authorizers and beneficiaries.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: A general accountability challenge may seek a culprit without mapping the people who support, permit and gain from a decision.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 records the director's approval and seeks other supporters; B4 exposes Sales as beneficiary, prompting A5 to investigate the space transfer's authorization.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.text: I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll need room to develop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm releasing equipment control so you can practice responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll surrender my override too. You must learn to make decisions without my safety net.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 provide credible corrections, but B mostly reports losses rather than pursuing an independent practical aim.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a chair's role and B4 supplies the playable nameplate, although the organization is unspecified.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 demands the cupboard key after correcting the election story; A3 turns that forced handover into a lesson in responsibility.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 requests administrator removal to change fixtures; A5 treats surrendering that control as deliberate removal of a safety net.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: Every reduction in A's actual control is narrated by A as a generous decision from a superior position.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: The concession grows from office to equipment to the remaining ability to override the successor.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D65 makes A describe involuntary losses of control as intentional concessions that demonstrate retained strength.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: D68 celebrates adversity as expanding influence, while D65 claims to have deliberately yielded the lost control.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 describes handing over a required key as releasing control for B's development; A5 claims removing A's administrator access is a deliberate withdrawal of superior protection.

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Act Authorized
cards.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stamped my request. The room's booked.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. A direct approval chain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't authorise yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to discuss why the stamp says approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the approved room request. Please put our rehearsal on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's your own stamp.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I process rehearsal approvals. You handle calendar entry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can hold the room while the manager confirms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use 'confirmed'; 'held' generates another approval request. Let's spare her a duplicate.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 challenge the stamp's legitimacy, but no concrete booking task or external check changes the exchange.

heightening.evidence: A5 returns to the stamp already established in A1 instead of adding a consequential procedure after B4.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'direct approval chain' turns B2's objection neatly, but A5's discussion is less active than the booking demand.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 notes that the stamp belongs to A; A3 treats that as normal evidence of A's approval-processing role.

cards.title: Rank Everything
cards.instruction: Turn every new contribution into a ranking that places you nearer the top.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

heightening.evidence: A5 accommodates B4's stronger claim by inventing a still higher role, then appropriates the exact piece B requested.

hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 introduces baking and claims the end piece; A5 elevates commissioning above baking and claims that same piece.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 repeatedly convert contributions into rankings that put A first.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 expands the hierarchy to absorb B's new qualification and turns superior rank into a specific material reward.

Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A3 and A5 rank both new contributions beneath an A-owned activity; logic 4, A3 uses B2's driving and A5 uses B4's baking and end-piece claim, although commissioning is newly asserted; relationship 4, B4 claims a concrete reward for making the cake; heightening 4, A5 moves from queue priority to taking the special portion B reserves; specificity 5, A1's picnic cake and B4's big end piece establish an immediate shared dispute; brevity 4, A5's commissioning claim directly earns the attempted appropriation. hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 converts personal displacement into a public display of expanding jurisdiction, using B's helpful solution.

cards.title: Access Has a Price
cards.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me

beats.text: I'll pay someone. I can't face painting over his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep them. Come help me tape around them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit with you. We can leave the paint unopened; I don't want us only meeting to empty his house.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 rejects interchangeable hired help through the shared pencil mark; A5 values being together despite poor painting.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's hiring solution with shared history, and A5 directly accommodates B4's lack of painting skill.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'tape around them' expresses care economically. A5's unopened paint earns the emotional turn, although its final explanation is more explicit than witty.

hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says participation may consist only of crying; A5 accepts that form of presence and removes the obligation to paint.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 and A5 make B's presence evidence that the connection survives beyond the practical work of clearing Dad's house.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 gives up the original task to secure the more vulnerable form of involvement B4 makes available.

mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Recruiting useful help would favor the competent painter that B2 proposes.

Separate internal re-read under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A1/A5 make continued contact the purpose of help; logic 5, B2's threatened marks cause A3's protective task and B4's anticipated crying causes A5 to give up painting; relationship 4, B2 offers money while B4 reveals the emotional barrier; heightening 4, A5 sacrifices the task to ask for a connection beyond estate chores; specificity 5, A1's kitchen and B2's height marks locate the encounter; brevity/wit 4, A5's unopened paint concretely expresses the changed priority without a separate joke. cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You know me. That's the qualification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might say the wrong thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say it in person. That's the bit I'm asking for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You survived every school play. I still want you in my corner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother will be there. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come before we open. I'll unpack the biggest piece with you. I want a memory of tonight with you in it too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 makes knowing A the qualification for attending, and A5 asks for personal presence even with an unsuitable comment.

specificity.evidence: A1's opening and ten-minute request combine with B2's sculpture reference to establish a playable invitation.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Say it in person' economically converts B4's exact objection into the desired commitment.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 requests Dad's attendance, A3 says 'I still want you in my corner,' and A5 seeks a memory containing him. Presence consistently signifies the relationship.

relationship.evidence: B2 presents discomfort about art, then B4 reveals the more consequential obstacle of encountering an estranged spouse. A5 changes the invitation to accommodate Dad.

heightening.evidence: B4 prompts A5 to replace brief public attendance with helping unpack the biggest piece, giving Dad a personal role in the opening.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies Dad and an opening; B2 establishes sculpture, and A5 provides an unpacking task. The venue and pre-opening access remain lightly sketched.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'survived every school play' supplies affectionate wit linked to B2's objection. A5's memory request is earned but somewhat polished.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 treats artistic knowledge as a prerequisite; A3 uses their school-play history to establish that parental support is enough.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 reveals the prospect of meeting Mum after the divorce; A5 offers a separate visit before public opening and a shared task.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A3 and A5 explain why this particular person's presence matters beyond attendance numbers or practical help.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 develops the request for ten minutes into a meaningful shared memory through active involvement.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D73 seeks attendance from a personally significant person as an expression of the connection.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The kitchen's spotless.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking about the people who cleaned it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What else needs doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sentence that lets me put my coat on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. I've done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Could you stay for the part that isn't the kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit with me for nine. I don't want the last thing we fixed tonight to be the sink.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 delays B's departure for relational repair, but A5 shifts to what will let A put a coat on.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes finished dishes and imminent departure; B2 keeps the kitchen situation concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'people who cleaned it' efficiently redirects B2's practical answer toward the relationship.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 explicitly separates completed dishes from an unrepaired relationship; A3 asks B to remain for the emotional work.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 acknowledges B2's completed cleanup; A5 uses B4's ten-minute bus limit to request precisely nine minutes.

relationship.evidence: B2 limits the commitment to cleaning and B4 needs the last bus; A5 accommodates that need while pursuing repair.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns a general request to stay into a bounded, urgent attempt at repair before the bus deadline.

specificity.evidence: A1's finished dishes and B4's last bus make both the practical release and remaining emotional urgency immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'part that isn't the kitchen' is concise; A5's sink callback is earned, though slightly polished for ordinary speech.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 says the agreed practical task is complete; A3 acknowledges this and asks for a different reason to stay.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 supplies ten minutes until the last bus; A5 bargains for nine rather than ignoring departure.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: The scene explicitly continues the effort to keep B present after the cleanup justification disappears.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 makes emotional repair time-limited and personally important while leaving B free to respond.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D74 keeps the other person present for relational repair after their practical reason to stay has ended.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Seeking reassurance alone could be satisfied later without trying to extend the current encounter.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 explicitly requests continued presence after B2 declares the cleaning complete, and A5 bargains for nine of B4's ten remaining minutes.

recommendedEdit: Revised the ambiguous coat exit and supplied a bounded departure cost. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3 requests staying beyond cleanup; logic 5, B2's completed task and B4's bus deadline determine A's requests; relationship 4, B has fulfilled a commitment and needs transport; heightening 4, A5 claims nine remaining minutes; specificity 5, dishes and the last bus are concrete; brevity/wit 4, A5's sink comparison grows from the cleaning. Total 92.

alternativeComparison: Alternative a bargains within B's travel constraint; b states that resolving the relationship takes priority over punctuality.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. We haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We finished the conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We stopped talking. That's a different task.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're going to make us late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather arrive late than leave like this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. We're packed, but we haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologised for telling my sister about your debt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay a minute. I can't face her checking what I order tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for dinner. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll be late. Sit with me and help me believe you're coming as my partner, not to report how grateful I am.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 holds off the taxi over last night's conflict, and A5 chooses lateness over departing unrepaired.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 contests B2's claim that the conversation is finished; A5 explicitly accepts B4's threatened lateness.

relationship.evidence: B2 considers the discussion complete and B4 wants to protect their shared arrival time.

heightening.evidence: B4 makes delay costly, and A5 accepts that cost rather than releasing the repair demand.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an imminent taxi and an unresolved previous-night exchange, though the destination remains open.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's distinction between stopping and finishing supplies a concise relational turn without extra explanation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 says packing is complete but prevents departure over last night's conflict. A5 explicitly accepts lateness to keep B present until partnership feels credible.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 reveals disclosure of A's debt, which A3 connects to scrutiny of dinner orders. B4 reveals prepaid dinner, which A5 connects to pressure to perform gratitude.

relationship.evidence: B2 believes an apology addresses the breach, and B4 presses their dinner obligation. A5 demands reassurance of loyalty, although B's own feelings remain mostly implicit.

heightening.evidence: B4's payment revelation makes the sister's involvement more immediate; A5 chooses lateness and asks B to establish allegiance before departure.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies the taxi and readiness to leave, while B2 and B4 establish debt disclosure and paid dinner. 'We're packed' leaves the wider travel situation unclear.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's fear of monitored ordering makes the injury concrete. A5's report of gratitude extends that fear coherently, though the sentence is comparatively long.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 names the disclosure of debt to the sister; A3 identifies the resulting fear of her judging tonight's spending.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says the sister has paid and departure is urgent; A5 accepts lateness and seeks reassurance that B will act as a partner rather than monitor gratitude.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 removes packing as a practical reason to stay; A3 and A5 continue holding departure open for relational repair.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 accepts an actual consequence, arriving late, and specifies the repair needed after B4 increases the sister's financial involvement.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D74 subordinates departure to feeling that the relationship has been repaired.

Added a disclosed debt and dinner with B's sister as illustrative context, retaining the taxi, unfinished previous-night argument and postponed departure used by the supplied pairs. cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Stay with that before explaining the train again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you saw me look at the door before the encore. Can you understand how it felt to keep expecting you?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks what the empty seat felt like; A3 rejects the transport explanation as a substitute for emotional acknowledgment.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's cancelled train directly, and A5 recognizes B4's 'let down' before asking B to remain with that understanding.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a credible reason for absence and B4 then identifies the hurt, changing A from eliciting acknowledgment to sustaining it.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends B4's acknowledgment rather than deepening its specificity or consequence substantially.

specificity.evidence: A1's missed concert and empty seat give the emotional cost a concrete, immediately playable image.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's timetable-versus-seat distinction compresses the disagreement into objects already supplied by A1 and B2.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 distinguishes an apology for absence from understanding the empty seat. A3 redirects logistical explanation, and A5 requests acknowledgment of repeatedly expecting B.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 redirects B2's cancelled-train explanation toward emotional impact. A5 uses B4's recording to identify looking at the door, but does not explicitly recognize B's partial acknowledgment.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a credible reason for missing the concert; B4 names disappointment and shows continued interest by watching the recording. A5 seeks more precise understanding.

heightening.evidence: B4's recording enables A5 to move from the general empty seat to a particular moment before the encore and the repeated experience of expecting B.

specificity.evidence: A1 immediately establishes a missed concert; B2 supplies the travel obstacle, and A5 provides a visible door glance before the encore.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'timetable' versus 'seat' compresses the conflict sharply. A5 earns its emotional specificity through B4, though the phrasing remains more poignant than comic.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 supplies a transport explanation; A3 specifically rejects discussion of the timetable as an answer to the emotional question.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 says the recording was watched; A5 uses that shared visual evidence to ask about a particular instance of continued hope.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 consistently seek recognition of the emotional cost rather than further explanation of the missed event.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 narrows 'let down' to the sustained expectation visible before the encore, adding specificity to the same demand.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D75 requires acknowledgment of the felt impact of an event beyond an apology or causal explanation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Demanding an admission of fault would contest whether the cancelled train excuses B's absence.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 does not dispute B2's train cancellation; revised A5 uses B4's watched recording to ask for recognition of repeated disappointed expectation rather than responsibility for the transport failure.

recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected original's static A5 and presumption of renewed defensiveness. Kept the concert setting and gave B4 a concrete act of involvement that A5 can use. Separate internal re-read under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A3/A5 seek felt impact beyond the transport explanation; logic 5, B2 prompts the timetable distinction and B4's recording prompts a specific visible moment; relationship 4, B4 both acknowledges hurt and demonstrates continued interest; heightening 4, A5 develops general disappointment into repeatedly expecting arrival during the performance; specificity 5, A1's seat and A5's door before the encore make the cost playable; brevity/wit 4, A3's existing contrast stays economical and A5 adds concrete evidence without an unrelated joke. Weighted total 92. Five spoken ABABA turns and causal hard gates pass on internal re-read.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
